true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the 4-arg version

Two `def self.downsize` methods are defined: the 4-argument `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145 and the 3-argument `(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at line 149. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 4-arg form no longer exists. Any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100)` now raises ArgumentError (or silently passes `100` as dimensions and `100` as opts). Keep one method, e.g. accept a dimensions string only, and update all callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings

`maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. Non-image attachments and sites with a different configured max size now get wrong client-side validation: files between the configured limit and 10MB are uploaded and then rejected by the server, and sites allowing >10MB attachments are blocked in the browser. The error message also reports a wrong limit to users.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsizing in place (from == to) can corrupt or truncate the tempfile

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` reads and writes the same path. ImageMagick's `convert` reading and writing the same file is unreliable, and the Ruby `Tempfile` object still has an open handle whose position/metadata is stale after the external process rewrites the file; `tempfile.size` and subsequent `Upload.create_for(... tempfile ...)` may see stale/incorrect data. Convert to a separate temp path and then replace/reopen the tempfile.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

false_positives.candidate:
413 error message reports a hardcoded, possibly wrong size limit

In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 branch now shows a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. If the web server or site setting limit differs, the user is told an incorrect maximum size.

Animated-GIF detection fails for tempfile paths

`OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. A Rails uploaded `tempfile.path` normally ends in a random suffix (e.g. `RackMultipart2014...`), not `.gif`, so animated GIFs will be processed with `convert ...[0]`, flattening animation to the first frame even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on. Detect the type from the original filename/content type instead.

Downsize loop ignores failures and can spin without progress

The while loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times but never checks its boolean return value. If convert fails (missing binary, unsupported file), the file size never changes and the loop just burns 5 shell invocations per upload, then proceeds to create an upload that will be rejected for size. Check the return value and break/report an error on failure.

Hardcoded 10.megabytes download limit replaces configurable setting

`FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was replaced by a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. Sites configured to allow larger images (or intentionally smaller limits) no longer have their setting respected for API URL uploads; this also bypasses an administrator-configured resource limit. Use a setting (e.g. a new max upload size setting) instead of a magic constant.

No tests for the new auto-downsize path

The new downsizing loop in `create_upload` (retry count, size threshold, non-image skip, failure handling) has no accompanying spec. Given it mutates the user's uploaded file in place, regressions would silently corrupt uploads.

Removal of public helper `self.dimensions` and signature change of `optimize`

`self.dimensions(width, height)` was removed and `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`. These are public class methods that plugins/other code may call; the change breaks them without deprecation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil

`self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. Creating/validating an EmbeddableHost with a nil host (e.g. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or the admin controller when `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of producing a validation error / 400. Guard with `return if host.blank?`. `sub!` also mutates the caller's string in place, which can raise on frozen string literals.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unknown id causes a 500 instead of 404 in update/destroy

`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host =` and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 error. Use `find_by` plus `raise Discourse::NotFound` (or `find`) so a deleted/invalid id yields a proper 404.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
record_for_host does not downcase the incoming host

The query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but `host` comes from `URI(x).host` without `.downcase`. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `EvilTrout.com`, which never equals the lower-cased column value, so a legitimately configured host is rejected (embedding returns InvalidAccess). Downcase the parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated host values are not normalized, so embedding breaks after upgrade

Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be of the form `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/1234` (the old code explicitly stripped schemes). The migration inserts the raw lines, bypassing the model's before_validation that strips scheme and path. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `URI(referer).host`, so rows like `http://example.com` will never match and previously-working embeds will start raising InvalidAccess after the upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator file contents swapped between files

`spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the category fabricators and `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` contains the embeddable_host fabricator. It works because all fabricator files are loaded, but it makes the definitions unfindable by name and will confuse anyone editing category fabricators. Swap the contents back.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Un-escaped interpolation of site setting value into INSERT

`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the old `embeddable_hosts` setting value straight into SQL. A host containing a single quote (data entered by an admin, or garbage left in the settings table) breaks the statement or allows arbitrary SQL execution during migration. Use `quote()`/bind parameters.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when `embed_category` site setting row is absent

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. On the vast majority of sites the `embed_category` setting was never set (no row in site_settings) or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration (and the whole deploy). Same risk on line 15 if `uncategorized_category_id` has no row. Use `.first` with a nil check / COALESCE instead.

false_positives.candidate:
New host with no chosen category shows no category badge

When adding a host without picking a category, `categoryId` stays null; the server defaults to uncategorized, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` (undefined), so the row renders an empty category cell until a reload. Use the category_id returned by the server response instead of the local `categoryId`.

No presence validation on category_id while the column is NOT NULL

The migration declares `category_id` NOT NULL but the model has no `validates_presence_of :category_id`. Only the admin controller patches in `uncategorized_category_id`; any other code path (fabricators, console, future callers) that saves without a category raises a raw ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation instead of a validation error.

`*_ids` hydration crashes on null or non-array values

The new branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with a plural suffix. If a serializer emits `foo_ids: null` (common for empty/absent associations) or a scalar, this throws TypeError and breaks hydration of the whole payload. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` / a null check; note `hydrated || []` after the map never helps because map always returns an array.

`create_table ... force: true` can silently drop an existing table

`force: true` issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If this migration is ever re-run, or a table named embeddable_hosts already exists, existing data is destroyed without warning. Drop the `force: true` option for a forward migration.

`update` is a no-op but is presented as a save action

`Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes the current state. The client's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6`) calls `embedding.update({})` and will appear to succeed while persisting nothing. Either implement the update or remove the route/action so admins aren't misled.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser record exists

`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for a user who has no topic_users row (e.g. notified via category watching, or a PM invite where the row was never created). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError (500) for a plain link click from an email. Use `TopicUser.change(...)`/`find_or_initialize` and handle the nil case.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
State-changing operation performed on a GET request

`unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a GET (route `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Mail clients, link scanners and browser prefetchers routinely fetch links in emails, which will silently mute topics without the user's intent. The mutation should happen on a POST/PUT (e.g. the landing page confirms, then posts), or be guarded by a one-time key.

Unsubscribe writes notification level directly, bypassing TopicUser.change

The action mutates `tu.notification_level` and saves the record directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`, so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not updated and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published. Any open browser tab or other client keeps showing the stale notification level. Also note the toggle semantics: a user already at `regular` gets muted, so a second click on the same email link silently mutes the topic — repeated/prefetched requests are not idempotent.

topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by topic.fromParamsNear

The `topic` resource (declared earlier, path `/t/:slug/:id`) contains `fromParamsNear` with path `/:nearPost`, which matches `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe` with nearPost="unsubscribe" before the later `topicUnsubscribe` route is considered. In-app transitions / client-side handling of the unsubscribe URL will therefore land on the topic route with a bogus post number instead of the unsubscribe page.

unsubscribe does not guard topic visibility explicitly and ignores JSON slug check

`TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is relied on for access control, but unlike `show` there is no `rescue Discourse::NotFound` / redirect-by-slug handling, so a stale or wrong-slug link produces a raw 404/500 instead of a redirect. Additionally, no spec covers this new endpoint (nil TopicUser, muted/watching transitions, slug mismatch redirect), so the above bugs are untested.

unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url} for every caller

The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` was updated to pass it. Any other `build_email` call with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (and all plugins/mailers doing so) will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, breaking those emails. Either make the second sentence conditional or default `unsubscribe_url` in `template_args`.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validator performs a DB write on every email validation, including valid?/preview calls

`BlockedEmail.should_block?` mutates and saves the matched row. Since `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` runs on every `valid?` call (e.g. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` before `user.save`), match_count can be incremented multiple times per signup attempt, making the statistic unreliable.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized

`BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` compares the raw submitted email. Emails stored in the table with different casing (or a user signing up with `Bad@Spamclub.com` when `bad@spamclub.com` is blocked) will not match, so the block is trivially bypassed. Normalize with `Email.downcase` on both write (before_validation) and lookup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for whitelist/blacklist paths moved into the new validator

The whitelist/blacklist logic was deleted from `User#email_validator` and moved to `EmailValidator`, but the new spec only covers the blocked-email branch. Any regression in the domain whitelist/blacklist behaviour (including the interaction where a whitelist/blacklist error suppresses the blocked check) would go undetected unless equivalent specs were moved too.

Signup failure response now echoes submitted attributes without restricting fields

`user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` plus `user.errors.to_hash` are returned in the failure JSON. This is fine for the three listed fields, but note the response now exposes the raw internal error keys; if more attributes are ever added to the slice (or the model gains sensitive attributes) they would leak to an unauthenticated endpoint. Consider returning only the explicitly needed values and documenting the contract, since the JS only uses `result.values.email`.

rejectedEmails array is shared between controller instances

`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` puts a single mutable array on the class prototype, so every CreateAccountController instance (and any re-instantiation of the modal) shares the same array. Emails rejected in one session/modal will keep being flagged as invalid afterwards, and the list is never reset. Initialize it per-instance (e.g. in `init`, or via a computed/`Em.A()` created on first use).

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
open-uri `open` on a URL permits pipe/file access and unbounded fetch

`open(url)` with Kernel#open semantics treats a string starting with `|` as a shell command and non-http strings as local file paths. Although TopicRetriever checks the host, `import_remote` is also called directly (disqus.thor, and `poll_feed` uses `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`), so a crafted feed URL setting can read local files or run commands. Use an explicit HTTP fetch (e.g. `URI.parse(url).open` after validating scheme) and bound the response size.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Weak postMessage origin check on the host page

`if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any origin that is a *substring* of the configured discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` or a prefix match), and it does not anchor at position 0. Any page able to postMessage can then resize the iframe. Compare the origin exactly against the origin component of discourseUrl.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise on render

The if/else block is terminated with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is a syntax error in Ruby (`if` used as a modifier with no condition), so compiling this template raises a SyntaxError and the `embed#best` action will 500 whenever a topic exists. It should be `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
poll_feed crashes when feed items have no `content`

`i.content.scrub` assumes every RSS/Atom item exposes `content`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `description`, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the job raises NoMethodError; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the whole polling run is lost. Also `String#scrub` requires Ruby >= 2.1. Fall back to `description`/`content_encoded` and guard against nil.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
request.referer interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript

`'<%= request.referer %>'` injects an attacker-controlled HTTP header directly into a JS string literal with no escaping. A referer containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x'+alert(1)+'`) breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary script in the Discourse origin, which also has the session cookie available. Escape with `j`/`javascript_escape` (or build the target origin from scheme+host only).

false_negatives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

false_positives.candidate:
Dead code: feed_key is computed but never used

`feed_key` builds a redis key for feed modification tracking but nothing reads or writes it, so the feed is re-parsed and re-imported in full every hour with no conditional-GET/ETag handling. Either implement the caching or drop the method.

Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` risks dropping top_topics

This changes an existing migration (which may already have run on deployed sites) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, i.e. drop-then-create. Any environment that re-runs or re-plays migrations loses the table and its data. Migrations should be immutable once shipped, and `force: true` should not be used here.

Missing embed_url raises ParameterMissing producing a 500 rather than a 400/404

`params.require(:embed_url)` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, which is not rescued here; unless the app has a global handler this surfaces as a 500 error with a backtrace rather than a clean 400. The accompanying spec only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it passes either way.

Raw rendering of posts whose cooked HTML is unsanitized remote content

`raw post.cooked` is emitted in the embed view, while `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `cook_method == :raw_html` (posts imported from RSS/readability). That means arbitrary HTML/JS pulled from a third-party feed is stored as `cooked` and rendered unsanitized inside a page on the forum's own origin. The imported HTML should be sanitized (whitelist tags/attributes) before being stored or rendered.

`force: true` in create_table will silently drop an existing table

`create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` first. If the migration is ever re-run (or the table exists for any reason), all topic_embeds rows are destroyed without warning. Remove `force: true` from migrations.

`import` mutates the caller's contents string

`contents << "...imported from..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache that string (and frozen-literal strings) will see corruption / RuntimeError. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

`open` used without requiring open-uri in topic_embed.rb

`import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file only requires nokogiri and ruby-readability. open-uri is only required in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, so when `import_remote` is reached via TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic without PollFeed having been loaded, `open` falls back to Kernel#open and will fail (or behave unexpectedly) on an http URL. Add `require 'open-uri'` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Header panel loses right alignment without flexbox support

`.panel`'s `float: right` was replaced by `margin-left: auto` + `@include order(3)`, which only work when the parent is a flex container. In browsers that don't support modern flexbox (where the `display: flex` fallbacks in the mixin resolve to the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` models that ignore `margin: auto`), the panel will be rendered left-aligned in normal flow, breaking the header. Also `.icons`/`.login-button` still use `float: left`, which is ignored on flex items, so those rules are now dead.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin mixes 0-based and 1-based ordinal values

`-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` are 1-based (default 1) while the standard `order` is 0-based (default 0). Passing the same `$val` to both means legacy box-model browsers compute a different relative ordering than standard-flexbox browsers (e.g. `order(2)` is one step from default in old syntax vs two in new). Either emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties or drop them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Floats inside new flex container are ignored in .small-action

`.small-action` now uses `@include flexbox()`, which makes its children flex items. `float` has no effect on flex items, so `.topic-avatar { float: left }` (line 270) and `button { float: right }` (line 309) no longer position as before — the button will no longer be right-aligned. Use `margin-left: auto` on the button (and remove the floats) to preserve the layout.

align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values for flex-* keywords

The mixin blindly forwards `$alignment` to legacy properties. `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` do not accept the modern `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords (they expect `start`/`end`), so any future `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently emit invalid declarations in the legacy prefixes while looking correct. Map values explicitly or drop the obsolete `-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align` lines.

inline-flex fallback ordering can override the better prefix

In `inline-flex()`, `-moz-inline-box` is declared after `-webkit-inline-flex`. If a UA understood both (and generally for cascade correctness), the older legacy value wins because it comes last. Legacy/box-model fallbacks should be listed before the newer prefixed and standard values, as done in `flexbox()`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing the trailing `?`

ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_website_name?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never called and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — including when `website` is blank (serialized as `null`). Rename to `include_website_name?`.

false_positives.candidate:
No test that website_name is hidden for untrusted users

The TL0/anonymous context asserts only the previously-listed untrusted attributes. Since `website_name` now derives from `website`, a spec asserting `json` has no `website_name` key for a restricted user is needed to lock in the privacy behaviour.

String literal mutation with `<<` in ends_with? comparison

`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on a string literal. It works today, but under frozen string literals (`# frozen_string_literal: true` or Ruby 3.x with the magic comment/`--enable-frozen-string-literal`) this raises FrozenError. Use `".#{website_host}"` instead.

URI parsed up to three times per call; website without scheme yields no name

`URI(website.to_s)` is re-evaluated in each branch (wasteful, and the second/third calls are not inside the rescue, so a malformed URI that raised once could raise unrescued later). Also, for a website stored without a scheme (e.g. `example.com/user`), `URI#host` is nil and the method returns nil, so no website is shown at all even though `website` is present. Parse once into a local and handle the scheme-less case.

website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking website for TL0 users to anonymous

`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` so it is hidden when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (TL0 user seen by anonymous). Fallback locales only loaded in web requests

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Because the translate_accelerator only lazily loads the yml for `config.locale`, any code path outside controllers (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console) that sets a locale will never load the fallback locale files, so fallback lookups return 'translation missing' instead of the default-locale/English string. The ensure_loaded! call should happen wherever the locale is set (e.g. in I18n.locale= or in the backend/translate path).

With fallbacks enabled, the result of `translate(key)` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (the second entry of the fallback chain), but the LRU cache key is only `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. In multisite (or after an admin changes the default locale) the same process can serve sites with different default locales, so a cached value resolved via site A's fallback locale will be returned for site B, producing wrong-language strings. Additionally the later check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` still uses the unclamped `offset`, so when clamping occurred the extra-row trimming is computed against the wrong expected length and an extra row may be returned on a page.

false_positives.candidate:
No test for the new in-insert eviction behavior

The PR's headline change (zset-based buffer with eviction of the oldest spans once a segment exceeds 1000 spans) has no test. Tests were only mechanically updated with `end_timestamp_precise`. A test asserting that a segment with >1000 spans keeps the newest 1000 (and what happens to the root span) is needed, since this path silently drops customer data if it misbehaves.

Redirect-chain limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, removing explanatory comment

The loop bound was lowered from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the consequence ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will now fail to be joined into a single segment, producing split segments, and the behavioral trade-off is no longer documented anywhere.

Span eviction limit hardcoded to 1000 and silently drops spans, ignoring max_segment_spans config

The eviction threshold `1000` is hardcoded in Lua while `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is now unused in Python, so the configured limit has no effect and the two can diverge. More importantly `zpopmin` removes the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise`, silently discarding span data from oversized segments without any metric/log (the previous code incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and skipped the segment). Oversized segments will now be emitted partially, and the dropped span may be the root/segment span, producing a segment with the wrong `is_segment` marking.

max_segment_spans is now dead config and missing from __reduce__

The span-count guard in `_load_segment_data` was removed, so `max_segment_spans` is no longer used anywhere; callers configuring it get no effect. Relatedly `__reduce__` still only passes `assigned_shards`, the two timeouts and `redis_ttl`, so `segment_page_size`, `max_segment_bytes` and `max_segment_spans` are reset to defaults when the buffer is pickled for multiprocessing — any non-default tuning is silently lost in the multiprocess consumer path.

span_count can be stale/incorrect when both unions execute

`span_count` is assigned from the first `zunionstore` and then possibly overwritten by the second, which is fine, but if only the first union runs and the parent merge is skipped, `span_count` reflects the cardinality *before* the current span's own zadd in some orderings; and if neither union runs `zcard` is queried. The net effect is that when a union happened, the count used for the `> 1000` eviction check can be lower than the actual set size (the new span payload is added by a separate pipeline step), so segments can exceed the intended cap or evict the wrong amount. Prefer always calling `zcard set_key` right before the eviction check.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Caching option-based allowlist in shared cache creates stale/incorrect results and cross-test pollution

`is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the allowlist eligibility in the global cache for 60s, keyed by org id and `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Problems: (1) the option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` change takes up to 60s to take effect, and the only invalidation helper (`invalidate_upsampling_cache`) is never called anywhere, so there is no real invalidation path; (2) `hash()` of a tuple is not a stable or collision-free key — different project sets can collide, giving a wrong eligibility answer for an unrelated project list; (3) the docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claims the config is read fresh every time, which the cache contradicts. Also the option lookup is already cheap/cached in Sentry, so the cache adds risk for no real gain. This also makes the new endpoint tests order-dependent/flaky, since tests mocking different allowlists for the same org+project set share the cache entry.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility uses outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`

`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` as a parameter but passes the outer-scope `dataset` to `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is intentionally called with a different dataset (e.g. `discover` for the errors-only query, or `split_dataset`), so the eligibility decision will be computed for the wrong dataset. Consequence: count() can be rewritten to `upsampled_count()` for a transactions-like query (where `sample_weight` is not meaningful/absent), or conversely skipped for a genuine errors query, producing wrong numbers or Snuba errors.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental git submodule/gitlink `sentry-repo` committed

The PR adds a gitlink entry `sentry-repo` pointing at `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This is clearly an accidental nested clone of the repository itself; it will break `git submodule` operations and clones for other developers/CI. Remove it before merge.

Blanket `except Exception: pass` silently drops invalid sample rates in test factory

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context read and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass`. A malformed `client_sample_rate` (e.g. a string, or contexts not being a dict) will silently leave `sample_rate` unset, making upsampling tests pass with regular counts and masking real bugs. At minimum narrow the exceptions (`AttributeError`/`TypeError`/`ValueError`) and/or assert in tests.

Cached value type not validated; truthy-return instead of bool

`cached_result` is returned as `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)`, which returns the cached object (not a bool) when it is falsy — e.g. returns `False`/`0` from the cache but with declared return type `bool`. More importantly the function is typed `-> bool` while potentially returning a non-bool cache payload. Callers compare it truthily today, but any `is True` check or typed consumer would break.

Duplicated upsampling transform logic invites divergence

`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is invoked in three separate branches (top_events, use_rpc, default) guarded by the same `upsampling_enabled` flag, each re-deriving `final_columns` from `query_columns`. The `should_upsample`/`upsampling_enabled` aliasing adds no value. Computing `final_columns` once right after the eligibility check would remove the risk of a future branch forgetting the transform.

Error-focused query detection by substring is unreliable

`_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check for `event.type:error` on the lowercased query string. This matches negated filters like `!event.type:error` and free-text/message content containing that string, and misses equivalent forms (`event.type:[error, default]`, `event.type: error`). For the discover dataset that means count() can be silently rewritten to `upsampled_count()` on queries that explicitly exclude errors, returning inflated counts. Use the parsed search query/filters instead of a substring match.

New endpoint tests mock `options` module-wide but do not clear the upsampling cache

These tests patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options`, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches eligibility in the shared cache for 60s under a key derived from org id + project ids. Because all tests in the class use the same org and project pair, whichever test runs first seeds the cache and the subsequent tests (partial allowlist, no allowlist) can read the stale eligibility value, making the assertions order-dependent and flaky. The tests need to flush the cache in `setUp`, or the caching should be removed.

Unused `organization` parameter and dead invalidation helper

`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes `organization` but never uses it, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called from anywhere in the codebase, so the cache added in this PR has no invalidation path. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or drop both.

upsampled_count relies on `sample_weight` column existing in discover/errors tables

The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction aggregates `sum(sample_weight)` with no guard. If the underlying Snuba table (discover/errors) does not have a `sample_weight` column, or it is NULL for non-sampled events, queries will either fail with a Snuba error or return 0/NULL counts for allowlisted projects. The code comment asserts the schema guarantees this, but nothing in this PR enforces it (the only place setting sampling data is the test factory, which writes `sample_rate`, not `sample_weight`). Consider a fallback such as `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` and declaring `default_result_type="integer"` to match the `toInt64` result.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
fetch_error_details pairs error ids with node values by position

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict whose value ordering matches the order of `error_ids`. That is an implementation detail of the backend (and of how it builds its result dict); if the ordering differs, each `ErrorEvent.id` will be attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing silently wrong summaries. Index by node id instead: build `node_id -> error_id` and look up `events[node_id]`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged TableWidgetVisualization branch renders a hard-coded empty table

When the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature, the table branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of passing the actual `result`/`fields`/`result.meta`. true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness

`validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` for truthiness. A report with `age: 0` (very common — a report generated just now) plus a `timestamp` will not be flagged, and `timestamp: 0` likewise. Use `is not None` / `in self.initial_data`. Also, neither field is required, so a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` passes validation entirely.

true_positives.golden_comment: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Analytics recorded before feature gate and schema validation

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has(...)` check and before request validation, so the event is emitted even for orgs without the feature (404 responses) and for malformed requests. Comment points at a migration that does not exist in this change

Both 0917 and 0920 now say "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no 0921 migration is added in this PR. Readers (and anyone auditing why the data migration was neutered) will look for a file that isn't there; either land the replacement migration in the same change or reword the comment.

Error/breadcrumb timestamps compared in different units

In `gen_request_data`, error timestamps come from nodestore event data (`data.get("timestamp")`, seconds since epoch) while rrweb replay events use millisecond epoch timestamps. The merge loop compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)` directly, so every error will always compare as earlier than every replay event and all error log lines will be emitted before any breadcrumb, destroying the chronological interleaving the function is meant to produce. One side needs unit normalization.

One invalid report rejects an entire browser report batch

Browsers send batches of reports to the Reporting API endpoint. The new loop returns 422 as soon as any single report fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same request. Since the browser will retry the whole batch, one malformed/unknown report type permanently blocks collection of the others. Prefer validating per report and skipping (with a metric/log) the invalid ones while returning 200.

dcg_to_slow_conditions now keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError

`get_condition_query_groups` previously computed slow conditions from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`, and `get_groups_to_fire` from `event_data.dcg_ids`. Both now receive a single map built from `event_data.dcg_ids`, and both still index it with `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]`. If `dcg_to_groups` contains any group id not present in `dcg_ids` (or `get_slow_conditions_for_groups` omits ids with no slow conditions rather than returning a defaultdict), this raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use `.get(dcg.id, [])` or assert the key sets are identical.

enabled guard `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is always true

`normalizeDateTimeParams` returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is unconditionally `true` and contributes nothing to the `enabled` condition. If the intent was to wait until page filters are ready, check `usePageFilters().isReady` or a specific field instead; as written the query may fire with default/unready filters.

get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue

`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the up-to-5 issues while building a PR comment. Each call is an additional snuba/nodestore + DB round trip inside a task that previously only used fields already loaded on the Group. This noticeably increases latency/cost for every merged-PR comment; consider batching or caching the environment lookup.

useTraceItemAttributeKeys can now return undefined attributes

Previously `attributes` was always a `TagCollection` (built with `useMemo` from `result.data ?? []`). It is now `isFetching ? previous : data`, where both `previous` and `data` can be `undefined` (first load, or when `enabled` is false / query errors). Callers doing `Object.keys(attributes)` or spreading it will throw at runtime. Default to `{}` or update the return type and all consumers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Component exported as `TwoFactor` in BackupCode.tsx

The default export in `BackupCode.tsx` is named `TwoFactor` (copy-paste from the TOTP component). This misleads readers and shows up as `TwoFactor` in React DevTools/stack traces for two different components. Rename to `BackupCode`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is a read-modify-write race

The backup code is validated and then invalidated via a separate `prisma.user.update` using the decrypted array read earlier. Two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either write lands, so a single backup code can be redeemed more than once (and the second write can also resurrect codes nulled by the first, since the whole array is re-serialized from stale data). Use an atomic conditional update or a transaction with row locking so each code can only be consumed once.

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
backupCodes state typed as never[] and blob URL never revoked

`useState([])` infers `never[]`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` and `backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode)` only type-check because the response body is `any`; any future typing of the response will break. Additionally the object URL created with `URL.createObjectURL` is only revoked when a new one is created — it is never revoked when the modal unmounts, leaking the blob (containing the plaintext backup codes) for the lifetime of the document.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup codes are overwritten on every setup call and can never be regenerated afterwards

`/totp/setup` unconditionally regenerates and stores new `backupCodes`, and `/totp/disable` nulls them. There is no endpoint or UI to view or regenerate codes once 2FA is enabled. Consequently, if the user closes the "Backup Codes" dialog (e.g. via the dialog X / `onOpenChange`) without copying or downloading, the codes are permanently unrecoverable while 2FA stays enabled, leaving the user with no recovery path. A regenerate endpoint (or showing codes again from settings) is needed.

Download button is nested in an anchor inside a form without type="button"

The download `Button` is rendered inside an `<a download>` which itself is inside the `<Form>` for `handleEnable`, and the button sets no `type` and no `preventDefault`. If the shared Button does not default to `type="button"`, clicking Download will also submit the enable form (re-running `handleEnable` with an empty totpCode) and may interrupt the download. Add `type="button"` explicitly, as done for the copy/close buttons via `preventDefault`.

No test covers logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The new authentication path (backup code verification in `next-auth-options.ts` and in `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`) including single-use invalidation is untested; the test only clicks the download/copy/close buttons on the setup screen (with TODOs for content). A regression that accepts an invalid code, fails to invalidate a used code, or breaks the backup-code login screen would not be caught.

[];` can yield `undefined`, and the next line dereferences it unguarded: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Use optional chaining.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback lookup is always undefined

`const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the `find` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares each `cal.externalId` against `undefined` and can never match. Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
BOOKING_CREATED/BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook assertions not updated for array payload

Only the BOOKING_REJECTED expectation was changed to `destinationCalendar: []`. The BOOKING_CREATED (line 119) and BOOKING_REQUESTED (line 373) expectations still assert `destinationCalendar: null`, but `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is now an array (`[]` or a list). These assertions will fail or, worse, pass accidentally and no longer verify the payload shape.

Dynamic booking user select lost `organization.slug`

The rewritten `loadUsers` drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic (no eventTypeId) user query that the previous code selected. Any downstream code relying on `user.organization?.slug` (e.g. booker/organizer URL construction for org users) will now see it missing for dynamic group bookings.

Legacy-reference cancellation path now deletes once per reference per credential

The loop over all `_calendar` references combined with the inner `else` branch (iterating every user calendar credential) means for N legacy references with M calendar credentials, M*N delete calls are issued, each using that reference's `uid`/`externalCalendarId` against unrelated credentials. This multiplies API calls and generates spurious 404s compared to the previous single-reference behavior.

Possible duplicate event creation for *_other_calendar destinations

After the destination loop, all credentials whose type includes `other_calendar` are unconditionally used to create another event. If a destinationCalendar entry points to one of those credentials (its `credentialId` matches, or its `integration` equals the credential type), the event is created twice for that integration, producing duplicate calendar entries and duplicate booking references.

Team destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null

`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when `destinationCalendar` is `null` (which happens when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar). In a collective event where only the non-organizer hosts have calendars connected, their calendars are silently ignored — exactly the case this PR aims to fix. Initialize to `[]` and push instead.

externalId not recorded for destinations without credentialId

In the `else` branch (destination without `credentialId`), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the third `externalId` argument, so `EventResult.externalId` is undefined and the booking reference gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` (line 169 now derives it from `result.externalId` instead of `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`). Subsequent updates/cancellations then cannot locate the event in the right calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fake literal "refresh_token" injected into credential keys

If the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the code assigns the literal string `"refresh_token"`. Callers store this value in the DB credential, so a real missing/omitted refresh token is replaced by a bogus value instead of preserving the existing one. Future refresh attempts will send `refresh_token=refresh_token` and fail with invalid_grant, requiring users to reconnect.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys are meaningless and strip required fields

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the same stringified object key (e.g. "[object Object]"), so the schema does not "assume any numeric property is the expiry" nor allow arbitrary extra properties. Because zod strips unknown keys by default, the parsed `data` when credential sharing is enabled contains only `access_token`, dropping `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and provider-specific fields. Callers then persist an incomplete credential key, breaking subsequent refreshes.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key stored as zod SafeParse wrapper object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)`, i.e. `{ success: true, data: {...} }`, not the parsed key. The previous code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned the key itself. The result is now written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` and will fail `googleCredentialSchema.parse` on the next use, breaking every Google Calendar connection after a token refresh.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential-sync path returns a fetch Response where callers expect axios/SDK shapes

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a `fetch` Response. Callers such as zoho-bigin, zohocrm (`tokenInfo.data.*`) and hubspot (expects a `HubspotToken` object with `expiresIn`/`accessToken`) read properties that do not exist on a `Response`. With syncing enabled those apps will throw or silently write `undefined` keys to the credential. The sync response must be normalized per-caller or parsed as JSON.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

Credential-sync path returns a fetch Response where callers expect axios/SDK shapes

When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` always returns a `fetch` Response. Callers such as zoho-bigin, zohocrm (`tokenInfo.data.*`) and hubspot (expects a `HubspotToken` object with `expiresIn`/`accessToken`) read properties that do not exist on a `Response`. With syncing enabled those apps will throw or silently write `undefined` keys to the credential. The sync response must be normalized per-caller or parsed as JSON.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
credentialId passed where userId is expected to the credential sync endpoint

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's id as the `userId` argument. The helper sends it as `calcomUserId` to the self-hosted sync endpoint, so the wrong user's credentials would be fetched/refreshed. `credential.userId` should be threaded through `refreshAccessToken` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fragile `response.statusText !== "OK"` success check

`statusText` is not guaranteed to be "OK" (it is empty on HTTP/2 and varies across runtimes/proxies), so successful refreshes can be rejected with a 400 HttpError. Check `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

Salesforce refreshes token on every client creation and then ignores the new token

`getClient` unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint on every service instantiation (no expiry check), which wastes a request and risks rate limiting. Worse, the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` / `instance_url` rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, so the refresh has no effect on the connection. It also bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce is excluded from the credential-sync feature this PR adds.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unvalidated input paths throw unhandled errors (500) and no HTTP method check

`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw, producing an unhandled rejection / opaque 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET included), so credentials could be mutated via a GET with a query-shaped body. Use `safeParse`/try-catch and restrict to POST.

false_positives.candidate:
APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string, not a boolean

The expression returns `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (string) or `undefined`/empty string rather than a boolean. It is consumed in boolean contexts and typed as such by consumers; wrap with `!!(...)` to avoid leaking the encryption key value into a client-importable constant module and to keep the type honest.

App slug "zoomvideo" does not match the Zoom app slug used elsewhere

`refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", ...)` sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the sync endpoint, but the app's slug in the DB/app store (and the value the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint looks up) is `zoom`. The shared secret is compared with `!==` against a header value, which is vulnerable to timing analysis, and `req.headers[name]` may be an array if the header is repeated (comparison then always fails/succeeds unpredictably). Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on normalized string values.

`prisma` is used but never imported in salesforce CalendarService

`prisma.credential.update(...)` is called in `getClient`, but there is no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"` in this file. This is a compile/runtime error (ReferenceError at request time), breaking every Salesforce calendar operation.

Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing bypass

"Add guests" action id/label mismatch and shown for past bookings

The new action uses `id: "add_members"` with label `t("additional_guests")`, which is inconsistent and makes the test id (`add_members`) misleading. More importantly, `editBookingActions` is also rendered for past and pending bookings (lines 553-554), so users are offered "add guests" on bookings that already happened, which triggers new CONFIRMED invite emails for a past event.

The catch block logs a fixed string via `console.log` and discards `err`, so email delivery/render failures for this new flow are effectively invisible in production. Use the project logger and include the error and bookingId.

MultiEmail imports from its own package barrel, creating a circular import

`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, while `packages/ui/index.tsx` re-exports `MultiEmail` (via MultiEmailLazy).
