No tests for the new addGuests mutation

This PR adds a new mutation that mutates booking attendees, updates external calendars and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization and filtering logic (team admin/owner check, blacklist, dedupe). No unit or e2e tests are included, so regressions in the permission check or the filtering cannot be caught.

Organizer email subject can render "undefined"/empty name

The subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. Newly added guests are created with `name: ""`, and if attendee ordering places a new guest first the subject becomes "Guests Added:  with  at ...". It also throws if `attendees` is empty. Fall back to the booker name/email as other organizer templates do.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders

The new OR branch in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` matches any WorkflowReminder with `retryCount > 1` regardless of `method`. Since this SMS cron runs globally, it will delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP workflow reminders as soon as some other code path increments their retryCount (and any future retry logic added for those methods), silently dropping pending reminders. The branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

false_positives.candidate:
Retry count not incremented when message/sendTo is missing

If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, the reminder is neither scheduled nor its retryCount incremented, so it will be re-picked by every cron run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the infinite-rescheduling problem this PR intends to fix (e.g. missing smsReminderNumber). Consider incrementing retryCount (or marking the reminder) in this case too.

deleteMany on retryCount has no supporting index

The new delete condition filters on `retryCount` alone (OR branch), which cannot use the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index and will force a full table scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron invocation. Scoping the condition to method/scheduled or adding an appropriate composite index would avoid this.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead branches in getBaseConditions mask an unreachable fallback

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null/undefined, and objects are always truthy), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This hides the intent: if auth conditions were ever intended to be optional, the fail-closed fallback would never trigger. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter, or make the types reflect reality.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Caching tests deleted without replacement

The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely. The caching logic still exists in the service (including the subtle `=== undefined` check that allows caching a `null` filter result), so this behaviour is now untested and regressions (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call) would go unnoticed.

Public `findMany` removed without updating callers

`InsightsBookingService.findMany()` was the only data-fetching entry point and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which merely returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No other files in this PR were updated, so any existing consumer calling `service.findMany({...})` will now fail to compile / throw at runtime. Either keep a `findMany` implemented on top of `$queryRaw`, or update all call sites in the same change.

Raw-query test asserts exact row shape that may not match driver output

`prisma.$queryRaw<{id:number}[]>` returns values with runtime types from the driver; if `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized.id` maps to a 64-bit integer the value comes back as `BigInt`, and `toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])` (a `number`) would fail. The PR description states the tests were never executed, so this assertion needs to be verified against an actual run.

Returned SQL fragments are not self-parenthesized, risking operator-precedence bugs

`buildFilterConditions`, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` can return top-level `OR`/`AND` expressions without surrounding parentheses (e.g. `"eventTypeId" = $1 OR "eventParentId" = $1`, or `(...) OR (...)` for team/org scope). `getBaseConditions` happens to wrap them, but `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` are public and documented as usable directly (the test interpolates conditions into `WHERE ${...}`). Any caller combining them with `AND` will get wrong, potentially authorization-bypassing results. Wrap each returned fragment in parentheses.

Widened constructor options type loses discriminated-union safety

The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `scope` is a plain union and `teamId` is optional. Previously the discriminated union forced `teamId` to be present for `scope: "team"`. Now `{scope: "team", userId, orgId}` type-checks, zod parsing fails silently, `this.options` becomes null, and every query degrades to `1=0` (empty results) with no error surfaced — a hard-to-diagnose data bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues a Prisma `updateMany` with an empty `data` payload. Prisma does not guarantee that an empty update bumps `@updatedAt` (and for some providers it is a no-op / can error), so the stated intent ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt") is not reliably achieved. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly. Additionally, for in-memory delegation credentials `this.credential.id` can be negative/non-existent, making this an unnecessary write on every cache refresh. The PR description itself notes this field isn't consumed anywhere in the UI, so it may be dead work.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a fragile relative .env path

`sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` interprets the empty string as the script argument and fails, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL rewrite silently errors for Linux contributors. Also `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the invocation directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` one level above the repository.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteCache rejects team/delegation credentials and throws generic Error

The handler only accepts credentials whose `userId` equals the session user, so calendar credentials owned by a team (userId null, teamId set) or delegation-derived credentials can never have their cache cleared, even though the UI renders the "Delete cached data" item for them (the dropdown only checks `delegationCredentialId` for the disconnect action, not for cache deletion). It also throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN"/"NOT_FOUND" })`, which surfaces as a 500 internal error and leaks the message as an unexpected server failure instead of a proper authorization response.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone

`new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's selected locale and time format preference, so non-English users see a US-formatted date inside otherwise translated text. Use the app locale (available via `useLocale`) and the user's `timeFormat`/timezone settings.

false_positives.candidate:
Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache shown as valid

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `MAX(updatedAt)` for all `CalendarCache` rows of a credential with no filter on `expiresAt`. Rows that have already expired (and are therefore never served) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports an active cache and a "Last updated" time for credentials whose cache is effectively dead. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

Migration warning comment contradicts the statement

The generated warning block says "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual statement does add `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning is misleading to anyone reviewing migration history; remove or correct it.

Repository instantiated directly, bypassing calendar-cache feature gating

The handler constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the path that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. This adds an unconditional DB `groupBy` on every connectedCalendars request even for installations/teams where calendar cache is off, and bypasses the mock abstraction the interface was designed for.

deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query

The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. When `onSuccess`/`onChanged` isn't supplied (it is optional and is undefined in some call sites), the UI keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful delete, suggesting the cache still exists. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in the mutation's `onSettled`.

dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx dependency

`dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in dependencies/devDependencies (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). `npx` will attempt an unpinned network install at run time, which fails offline/CI and gives a non-reproducible version. Add `tsx` as a devDependency (and drop `ts-node` if no longer used).

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but invoked inside `forEach` without awaiting; the handler returns a 200 "Booking successfully cancelled" before the `cancelled: true` DB updates complete. In a serverless environment the function may be frozen/terminated before the updates are persisted, leaving reminders uncancelled. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all`.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete path leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB

In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, when `immediateDelete` is true the function cancels the scheduled send at SendGrid and returns without deleting (or updating) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers that use this path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflows.tsx workflow/step deletion) therefore leave orphaned reminder rows with `scheduled: true` and a now-unusable `referenceId`. The row lingers until the cron's `deleteMany(scheduledDate <= now)` eventually removes it, and because `referenceId` is `@unique` a stale row can also block reuse. The non-immediate path at least marks `cancelled: true`; the immediate path should delete the row.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cancellation query is not restricted to EMAIL reminders or non-null referenceId

`remindersToCancel` selects every `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now+1h`, without filtering `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Any non-email or reference-less row that ends up with `cancelled: true` would be sent to the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint with a null/foreign batch_id, which errors and (per the finding above) aborts the whole batch.

PrismaPromise imported as a runtime value

The import was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that includes `PrismaPromise`. `PrismaPromise` (and `Prisma` as used here) are type-only exports of @prisma/client; importing them in a value import can fail at build/runtime with isolatedModules/SWC transpilation ("PrismaPromise is not exported"). Keep these as `import type`.

Reschedule path still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, so the bug being fixed persists for reschedules

The PR's stated fix is to avoid SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellation limit by deferring cancellation to the cron (`cancelled: true`). However the reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete = true`, which issues the `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel immediately. Reschedules will therefore keep accumulating pending cancellations and can still fail once the limit is reached, meaning reminders for rescheduled bookings are still sent — exactly the reported issue (#7225) for the reschedule case. The same applies to workflow/step deletion in workflows.tsx.

Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders

The cancellation loop is wrapped in one `try/catch` and `await`s the SendGrid request inside the loop. If any single `client.request` throws (e.g. invalid/expired batch_id, rate limit), the catch is hit and all remaining `remindersToCancel` in this run are skipped. Since the cancellation window is only 1 hour and the cron runs every 15 minutes, repeated failures on the same bad reminder will permanently prevent later reminders in the list from being cancelled, and their emails will be sent. The try/catch should be per-reminder inside the loop.

Unscheduled-reminder query does not exclude cancelled reminders

The `unscheduledReminders` query filters on `method: EMAIL, scheduled: false` but not `cancelled`. A reminder that was scheduled far in the future (stored with `scheduled: false`) and then cancelled on booking cancellation/reschedule will still be picked up by this cron and scheduled with SendGrid, so a reminder for a cancelled booking gets sent. Add `cancelled: null` / `not: true` to the where clause (or delete such rows).

try/catch cannot catch failures of the un-awaited async calls

The `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)) } catch` block cannot catch errors from these promises since they are not awaited; a rejection would surface as an unhandled rejection rather than the intended `log.error`. Await the promises inside the try.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
apiDeletes is populated inside an async forEach callback and is never awaited for recurring cancellations

In the recurring-booking branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` returns immediately; the awaits inside resolve after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` has already run with an empty/partial array. Calendar deletions for remaining recurring instances are therefore unobserved: failures are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the response can be returned before any event is deleted. Use a `for...of` loop with `await`, or push the promises (not awaited results) synchronously.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Commented example path is wrong

The placeholder comment reads `// example: import("./example")`, but the example app lives in `_example` (the previous code commented `import * as example from "./_example"`). Anyone uncommenting it will get a module-not-found error.

Eagerly created import promises can produce unhandled rejections

Because all ~28 dynamic import promises are created at module load, a failure in any single app module (missing dependency, throwing top-level code) results in a rejected promise that nobody awaits unless that specific app is used. In Node this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection and can terminate the process, even for apps the request never touches. Deferring the import until the app is requested avoids this.

appStore map invokes import() eagerly, so nothing is actually lazy-loaded

Each property is initialized with `import("./app")` evaluated at module-evaluation time, so importing `@calcom/app-store` immediately starts loading every app package (and bundlers will include them all in the graph). The only change versus the previous static imports is that consumers must now `await`; there is no deferral and no bundle-size/cold-start win. To get the intended async behaviour the values must be thunks (e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) resolved on demand.

forEach with async callback escapes the surrounding try/catch and is not awaited

Same problem as the vital variant: the async callback passed to `forEach` is not awaited, so errors from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` bypass the enclosing try/catch (becoming unhandled rejections) and cancellation of the external calendar/video events may not have happened by the time the function returns true and the email is sent.

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the `calendar` field, breaking external consumers

`getCalendar` is now async, so `getCalendarCredentials()[n].calendar` is a `Promise<Calendar | null>` rather than `Calendar | null`. Only `getConnectedCalendars` was updated (it awaits `item.calendar`). Any other caller of `getCalendarCredentials` that uses `.calendar` directly (e.g. API/trpc handlers for connected calendars, availability code) will now silently operate on a Promise object, producing runtime errors or truthy-but-useless values. All call sites need auditing/updating.

requestReschedule fires un-awaited async forEach for calendar/video deletion

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { await getCalendar(...) ... })` creates floating promises. The mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns to the client while the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls may still be pending, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no logging. Await the deletions (for...of or Promise.all) before proceeding.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start, not the slot end

In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intent is clearly to compare the slot's end time (`start + eventLength`) against `workingHour.endTime`. As written, a slot that begins inside working hours but ends after them is treated as available, so bookings can overrun the host's availability. (The condition is also an OR of two checks inside a `.find()` whose truthiness means "outside working hours", so the duplicated value silently disables the end-boundary check.)

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false

`if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intended "unavailable/zero-length override" case (start equals end, i.e. the whole day marked unavailable) is therefore never detected, so slots on a fully-blocked override day are not rejected here. Use `.isSame(...)`.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override short-circuits the busy/booking check, so booked slots become available

When any date override matches the slot's date, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` immediately (line 133-135), skipping the `busy.every(...)` loop below. Consequently, on a day that has a date override, existing bookings, calendar busy times and reserved slots are ignored and already-occupied slots are offered as available, leading to double bookings. The busy check must still run after override-boundary validation.

Date overrides of all users are applied to every host's availability check

`checkIfIsAvailable` receives the per-user `schedule` spread (`...schedule`) for fixed hosts, but the `dateOverrides` list built at line 410 is the flattened list of overrides for *all* users (it carries `userId`), and the override matching at line 106 never filters by `userId`. An override belonging to one host therefore sets `dateOverrideExist`/rejects slots for a different host, producing wrong availability for team events.

No test for the PR's main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)

The PR claims to fix that date overrides of fixed hosts are honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (issue #8207/#8329), but the only added test re-runs the existing single-user date-override scenario with a different invitee timezone and expects identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host with a date override and an available round-robin host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` date-override/working-hours logic for fixed hosts is untested and regressions would go unnoticed.

Override start/end converted with hour()*60+minute() loses day rollover

After applying `offset`, the start/end are reduced to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. If the timezone offset pushes the override across midnight (common for large offsets, e.g. an organizer override near the end of the day viewed from a far-west/east invitee timezone), the resulting `startTime` can exceed `endTime`, and `buildSlots` skips such ranges (`if (start >= end) continue`). The override day then shows no slots at all instead of the shifted window.

`override.timeZone` is optional; undefined falls back to server local timezone

`TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, and `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` resolves to the process-local timezone. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not populate `timeZone` on date overrides (all callers other than the trpc slots router) will compute `organizerUtcOffset` from the server timezone, silently shifting overrides by an arbitrary amount. Either make `timeZone` required for overrides or fall back to an explicit organizer timezone.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
KeyError when integration metadata has no 'sender'

`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the `sender` key always exists. `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when the pipeline state contains `sender` (i.e. when the installation webhook was processed), so pre-existing Integration rows and installs where the webhook didn't populate sender will raise KeyError/TypeError, producing a 500 error instead of the intended friendly failure page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and treat a missing value explicitly.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
No test for missing/failed access_token exchange or missing sender metadata

The new failure branches in OAuthLoginView (token exchange returning no `access_token`, `get_user_info` returning no `login`) and the GitHubInstallation branch where `integration.metadata` lacks `sender` are untested. Given these are the security-critical paths this PR adds, tests covering a failed/reused `code` and a metadata-without-sender integration should be added.

Non constant-time comparison of pipeline signature

`request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` compares a user-supplied value against a secret-derived signature with `!=`, which short-circuits on the first differing byte. Use `django.utils.crypto.constant_time_compare` to avoid leaking information about the signature through timing.

get_user_info failure is unhandled

`get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called outside any try/except. If GitHub returns a non-200 (revoked token, rate limit, outage) this raises (e.g. ApiError) and the installation flow returns an unhandled 500 rather than rendering the github-integration-failed page like the other failure branches. It also assumes the return value is a dict supporting `in`.

test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 installation path

The test now sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature, so the request fails at the new state check in OAuthLoginView and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." message. The original assertion ("The GitHub installation could not be found." from `build_integration` on a 404 from /app/installations) is therefore no longer exercised at all; that error path is now untested. Use the correct state so the flow actually reaches the installation lookup, and add a separate test for state mismatch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`queued` default evaluated once at import time

`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a class-level default evaluated when the module is first imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the process start time instead of the actual creation time. This makes the field useless for diagnosing/ordering sync events (and misleading in logs). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Non-JSON-serializable datetime passed in Celery task kwargs

`assignment_source.to_dict()` (via `dataclasses.asdict`) includes the `queued` datetime object, which is placed into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. With a JSON task serializer this raises a serialization error and the outbound assignee sync task is never queued, silently breaking all outbound assignee syncs whenever an assignment_source is present. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (and parse it back in `from_dict`).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

false_positives.candidate:
New `assignment_source` kwarg may break existing sync_assignee_outbound implementations

The task now always passes `assignment_source=...` to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound`. Concrete implementations (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, GitHub Enterprise, etc.) whose signatures are `(self, external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs)` are fine, but any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise TypeError at runtime. The abstract signature in `mixins/issues.py` was not updated to include `assignment_source` either, so implementers get no signal. Add the parameter to the abstract signature and verify every override accepts it.

from_dict does not validate/convert field types

`from_dict` simply splats the dict into the constructor, so a round-tripped `queued` string stays a `str` and `integration_id` could be any type (e.g. a string from JSON), with no error. Downstream comparisons like `sync_source.integration_id == org_integration.integration_id` would then fail silently (string vs int), defeating the cycle-breaking logic. Coerce/validate types explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and will raise TypeError on instantiation

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since none are implemented, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` remains abstract and `Detector.detector_handler` (which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` whenever a metric alert detector is processed. false_positives.candidate:
Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread

`_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(...)` (ultimately arroyo's `commit` passed to `create_with_partitions`). Arroyo's commit callback and the underlying Kafka consumer are not thread-safe and are expected to be called from the strategy/processing thread (the same thread that calls `poll`/`submit`). Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's own consumer operations can corrupt consumer state or crash librdkafka. Offsets should instead be accumulated and committed from `poll()`.

Decode/submit failures are silently acked instead of DLQ'd

In `submit`, any exception (including the `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` and the `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` inside `decode_payload`) is swallowed and the offset is immediately marked added+complete, so the message is committed as if processed. This drops messages without routing them to the DLQ and will also silently discard every `FilteredPayload` while logging an exception for each. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly and genuine failures should be surfaced/DLQ'd rather than acked.

No final commit on close(), and offset state survives rebalances

`close()` sets `shutdown_event` (ending `_commit_loop` without a last pass) and then shuts the pool down after workers drain remaining queued items. Offsets for everything processed since the last 1-second tick, plus everything drained during shutdown, are therefore never committed, so those messages are reprocessed after restart. Additionally `OffsetTracker` state (`all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed`) is never reset on partition revocation; because the pool/tracker is shared across `create_with_partitions` calls, a new strategy can commit offsets for partitions the consumer no longer owns. A final `get_committable_offsets()`/commit after draining, plus per-assignment tracker reset, is needed.

Transaction name hardcodes "monitors" prefix for generic remote-subscription consumer

The sentry_sdk transaction is named `f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}"`, but this strategy is generic to remote subscriptions (uptime being the first user). Uptime traffic will be reported under a `monitors.*` transaction name, making performance data misleading.

Unbounded queues provide no backpressure despite docstring claim

`queue.Queue()` is created with no maxsize and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but in practice a slow group can accumulate unbounded work items (each holding the decoded result and the original Kafka `Message`), growing memory without limit and making the uncommitted offset window unbounded. Set a maxsize and raise `MessageRejected` when full so arroyo throttles consumption.

queue.ShutDown / Queue.shutdown require Python 3.13

`queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown(immediate=...)` were added in Python 3.13. On an older interpreter the module-level reference raises `AttributeError` at worker runtime and `q.shutdown()` is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`, leaving workers blocked forever in `work_queue.get()` and making shutdown hang for 5s per worker. If the project must support <3.13, use a sentinel item to stop workers instead.

queue_pool is created once per factory but destroyed on strategy close, breaking processing after a rebalance

`FixedQueuePool` is constructed once in `__init__` and reused by every `create_with_partitions` call. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which permanently stops the worker threads and shuts down the queues. Arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again after every partition revoke/assign (rebalance), so the second strategy will be handed a pool whose workers are dead and whose queues raise `ShutDown` on put. From then on the consumer silently accepts messages that are never processed and never commits, i.e. it stalls permanently until the process is restarted. The pool needs to be created per strategy (or recreated when it has been shut down).

true_positives.golden_comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Every negative Check for a new resource name triggers a full permission DB query

Check now falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB query for basic roles, teams and permissions) whenever the cached scope map does not grant access, and only caches the negative result per (namespace, user, action, name, parent). Since `name` is caller-supplied, a client repeatedly checking distinct resource names the user cannot access produces one full permissions query per distinct name within each 30s window, bypassing the permission cache entirely. This is a significant and attacker-influenceable increase in DB load compared to the previous behaviour where the cached scope map answered denials. Consider caching a "permissions freshly loaded" marker per user/action so at most one DB refresh happens per TTL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Denial-cache test does not actually prove the denial cache short-circuits

The test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" claims to "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but it seeds the permission cache with `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, i.e. the scope maps to false, so `checkPermission` would deny anyway (and with no store configured the fallback path would also deny). The test therefore passes even if the permission-denial cache lookup were removed entirely, so the new behaviour is untested. Set the scope to `true` so that a deny result can only come from the denial cache.

true_positives.golden_comment: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Denial cache key can collide between distinct (name, parent) pairs

`userPermDenialCacheKey` joins namespace, user, action, name and parent with a single `_` separator and name/parent are arbitrary UIDs that may contain `_`. For example name="a", parent="b_c" and name="a_b", parent="c" produce the same key, so a denial recorded for one resource can deny a different resource for up to the cache TTL. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs or length-prefix the components.

false_positives.candidate:
Denial cache delays visibility of newly granted permissions with no invalidation path

A negative result is cached for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) keyed per resource, and nothing invalidates it when a permission is granted (e.g. a user is added to a role/team or given access to an existing dashboard). Previously such a grant became visible when the per-user permission cache expired; now the deny answer is sticky for up to 30s after the grant with no way to clear it. Worth documenting, or wiring an invalidation on permission writes.

permissionCacheUsage metric records a miss on cache hits that denied

When `getCachedIdentityPermissions` succeeds but `checkPermission` returns false, execution falls through to line 137, which increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label "false" (miss) even though the permission cache was actually hit. The cache hit-rate metric will therefore understate hits for all deny paths, making it unreliable for tuning the cache.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Concurrent requests (same instance or multiple Grafana instances sharing the DB) can all read count < deviceLimit and then each insert a new device, exceeding the configured limit by an arbitrary amount. Also, a COUNT(*) query is now executed on every tagged request, adding DB load on the authentication hot path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

With MySQL, UPDATE reports the number of *changed* rows, so an existing, known device whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at values are unchanged (e.g. repeated requests within the same second, since MySQL datetime precision is seconds) yields 0 and the user is wrongly rejected as over the device limit even though the device is already tracked. true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. When the device limit is reached and CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry remains, so every subsequent request with the same device id returns nil early (for the 29-minute cache TTL) and the anonymous client authenticates successfully. The limit is therefore enforced only for the first request of each new device and then effectively bypassed, and behaviour differs per Grafana instance (each has its own local cache). New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented and missing from defaults.ini

cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit, but conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini and the anonymous-auth documentation are not updated in this PR. Users have no discoverable way to learn about or configure the new limit, and the setting won't appear in the shipped config files.

Raw ErrDeviceLimitReached returned from Authenticate yields an opaque 500

ErrDeviceLimitReached is created with fmt.Errorf and returned directly from Authenticate. The authn layer has no status mapping for it, so a user hitting the device limit gets a generic internal error instead of a meaningful message/status (e.g. errutil with 429/403 and a user-facing message). true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete passes object name as the 'kind' metric label

`d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource `name` where every other call site passes `options.Kind`. This both mislabels the metric and causes unbounded label cardinality (one time-series per object name), which can blow up the Prometheus registry.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes derive from request context and get cancelled

All four goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) build their timeout context from the incoming request `ctx`. The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which typically happens before the goroutine completes its legacy write. The legacy store write will therefore frequently be aborted mid-flight, silently losing the data that mode 3 is supposed to keep in sync. Use a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context carrying the needed request values) before applying the timeout.

Storage failure recorded as legacy duration in Create/Update

In Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) the error path for the *storage* call calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. This attributes unified-storage failures/latency to the legacy backend metric, making the dashboards and error rates for both backends wrong. Should be `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

Tests never synchronize with the async legacy write (data race + no coverage)

Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection in mode 3 spawn a goroutine that calls the legacy mock. The tests return immediately after the call, so (a) the legacy write is never asserted — mode 3's core behaviour is untested, and (b) the shared `*mock.Mock` is read/written concurrently by the goroutine and by the test's assertions/teardown, which `go test -race` can flag as a data race and causes intermittent panics (mock calls after test completion). Add a synchronization point (e.g. wait channel from the mock's Run/ `assert.Eventually`) and assert the legacy call happened.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock

After the RLock fast path fails, the code takes the write lock but does not re-check `entryPointAssetsCache`. Under concurrent startup load, N goroutines queued on the write lock will each re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json even though the first one already populated the cache. Add a double-checked `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return ... }` after acquiring the lock.

true_positives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache is overwritten with nil/partial result on error

`entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed unconditionally, even when `err != nil` and `result == nil`. A transient failure (e.g. CDN/file read error) therefore clears a previously valid cached value, forcing every subsequent request to re-read the manifest and potentially return errors. Only assign the cache when `err == nil && result != nil`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions contains unreachable/dead logic and always returns false

`enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the inverted logic), then returns false in both branches. The feature-toggle read has no effect and the inverted expression is misleading: a future reader may 'fix' the branch and accidentally re-enable SQL expressions when the flag is *disabled*. If the intent is to hard-disable the feature, the function should simply `return false` (or the QueryTypeSQL case should error unconditionally) with a comment explaining the CVE; the dead flag check should be removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Misleading error message for disabled SQL expressions

Returning "sqlExpressions is not implemented" to users who have the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle enabled is confusing, since the feature previously worked and the toggle still exists and is documented. The message should state that SQL expressions are currently disabled/unavailable so operators don't file bugs about a toggle that silently does nothing.

false_positives.candidate:
No test asserting SQL expressions are disabled

This PR is a security fix that disables a code path leading to RCE/LFI, but adds no test. A regression test asserting that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error (even with the `sqlExpressions` toggle enabled) and that `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto`/`RunCommands` return errors would prevent an accidental re-enable of the vulnerable path.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent builds of the same index key

BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its whole body, which serialized index creation. Now only the cache write is locked, so two callers for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a watch event handler plus startup build, or two concurrent search requests that both see a nil index via GetIndex) can run bleve.New() against the same on-disk directory concurrently. bleve.New fails or corrupts state when the directory already exists/is open, and the second winner overwrites the cache entry while the first index is still referenced by a caller. Some per-key coordination (e.g. a keyed mutex / singleflight) is needed, not just a cache-write lock.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TotalDocs reads b.cache without holding cacheMu

TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no lock while BuildIndex now writes to the map under cacheMu from worker goroutines and from the watch-event path. Concurrent map read/write panics the process. This is newly reachable because search.init() now logs s.search.TotalDocs() and index builds can be triggered asynchronously by the watch goroutine. Take cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs.

false_positives.candidate:
Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks the server context and background resources

When s.Init(ctx) returns an error, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling cancel() on the context created above (and without stopping any lifecycle/blob resources already initialized). The context and any goroutines started during partial init (e.g. the storage watch poller started by backend WatchWriteEvents) are leaked for the life of the process. Call cancel() (and ideally s.Stop) before returning the error.

Postgres path of the storage-server integration test is now skipped

The only integration test exercising the storage server target is disabled for postgres with a TODO. Since this PR changes initialization to happen eagerly at ResourceServer construction (the riskiest behavioral change here), the test that would catch startup regressions no longer runs on postgres in CI, leaving that configuration uncovered.

Shared `err` variable written from concurrent errgroup goroutines

Inside the `for _, info := range stats` loop, each goroutine assigns to the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and also increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed` counter without synchronization. With initWorkers > 1 these are concurrent writes to the same variables — a data race that can be detected by -race and can mask or mis-report build errors (one goroutine's error being overwritten by another's nil). Use a goroutine-local `err :=` and an atomic counter.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias

`getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the actual alias (`idp-alias-<i>` / `idp-alias-20`). The 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are therefore never removed (and the cleanup call will fail with 404), leaving leftover IDPs in the realm that can make other tests in the class or run order flaky. Same problem at lines 381 and 425 (and the pre-existing line 303).

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
getForLogin cache not invalidated/bypassed when the organization changes

Unlike `getByOrganization`, which checks `isInvalid(orgId)` in addition to its own cache key, `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If an organization is disabled or removed in the same transaction (or its invalidation is registered under the org id), the ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists remain served from cache and still contain the organization's IDPs. Callers that don't re-check `isEnabled()` on the returned wrapped models (only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean does) will show IDPs of a disabled/removed organization on the login page. Consider also bypassing the cache when `organizationId` is invalidated, and registering login-cache invalidation on organization updates/removal.

getLoginPredicate can NPE on IDPs with null config

The new predicate calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` whenever `getOrganizationId() != null`. `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is not guaranteed non-null (e.g. models built from partial representations or imports), so a NullPointerException can be thrown from create/update/remove paths that call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, breaking the IDP write operation. Use a null-safe access on the config map.

remove() now always issues a DB lookup by alias

Previously `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only executed on the invalidated-cache path; now it is executed unconditionally before deciding, adding an extra database query to every IDP removal even when the entry is cached. It also means the cached-path branch computes `storedIdp` it doesn't use. Consider reusing the cached model for the login-invalidation check.

true_positives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls

Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the integers and discard the results; they have no effect since the DER sequence is built on lines 117-121. Remove them to avoid confusion (and wasted allocations).

true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Indefinite-length sequence silently decodes as empty list

`readLength()` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). In `readSequence()` the loop `while (length > 0)` is then never entered, so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE returns an empty list instead of an error, and callers then throw a confusing "Invalid sequence with size different to 2" or mis-handle it. Reject length < 0 explicitly in readSequence/readInteger.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
New abstract `order()` method breaks external CryptoProvider implementations

`int order();` is added as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. Any third-party or downstream implementation (e.g. in the keycloak-client repo, adapters, custom FIPS providers) will fail to compile and will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when loaded via ServiceLoader. Give it a `default` implementation (e.g. `return 100;` or 0) to keep the interface backward compatible.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

false_positives.candidate:
Ambiguous provider selection no longer fails fast and is logged only at debug

Previously having multiple `CryptoProvider`s on the classpath threw `IllegalStateException`. Now the highest `order()` wins, but `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return 200, so if two of them are on the classpath (a real misconfiguration, e.g. default + fips) the choice is arbitrary/ServiceLoader-order dependent and silently proceeds, only noted via `debug` logging. Consider distinct orders and/or a warn-level message when two providers share the top order.

Test only round-trips its own encoder and uses a wrong-size key for ES384/ES512

The key pair is generated with the JDK default EC curve (typically P-256) yet the test runs with `ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384`/`ES512` signature lengths, so the signatures are not representative of those algorithms. Additionally the assertion only compares the decoder's output with itself after re-encoding, so a systematically incorrect DER encoding (e.g. missing padding or wrong tags) would still pass. The test should use the proper curve per algorithm and verify interoperability, e.g. compare against the BouncyCastle-based `BCECDSACryptoProvider` output and/or verify the re-encoded DER with `Signature.verify()`.

getKeyStore uses enum name() instead of toString() unlike other providers

All other CryptoProvider implementations call `KeyStore.getInstance(format.toString())`. `KeystoreFormat` overrides `toString()` (the JCA type string may differ from the enum constant name, e.g. for PKCS12/BCFKS variants), so using `format.name()` here can request a nonexistent keystore type and make `getSupportedKeyStoreTypes()` report wrong results. Use `format.toString()` for consistency.

logger.debugf called with a dynamic string as format

`logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built string as the format template. If any class name or future content contains a '%' character this throws/misformats (java.util.IllegalFormatException). Use `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` with the value as an argument.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removal cleanup listener now skipped when neither FGAP v1 nor v2 flag matches

registerListener's body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. Previously the role/client/group removal handlers always ran, cleaning up leftover authorization policies for deleted roles, clients and groups created while v1 was enabled. After this change, if an installation disables the v1 feature (e.g. switches to v2) any pre-existing v1 permission policies for removed roles/clients/groups are left orphaned in the database. If the gating is only meant to avoid the UnsupportedOperationException thrown by the new V2 classes, gate on "v2 not enabled" or make the V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission includes the aggregate 'Clients' resource in the result set

resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) matches every resource whose type is "Clients", which includes the schema-created aggregate resource named "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name == type == "Clients"). If a permission is granted on the aggregate resource, the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set of client ids. Callers interpret these entries as client identifiers, so this yields a bogus id (and, conversely, granting an all-clients permission does not expand into the actual client ids). Filter out the resource whose name equals the resource type and handle the all-clients case explicitly.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Possible NPE when the 'Clients' resource-type resource cannot be resolved

In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the client, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...). That method returns null when the realm's authorization schema is not supported/enabled or the resource was not found. The returned value is passed straight into policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and then dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a null result causes a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access. Add a null check returning false.

true_positives.golden_comment: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead code and unused imports in new class

getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is private and never called, and the `logger` field, the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE and the imports of Scope/ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext are unused. This dead code was presumably copied from ClientPermissions (token exchange) and should be removed to avoid suggesting token-exchange evaluation is supported here (canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException).

false_negatives.golden_comment: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

false_positives.candidate:
getResourceName has no branch for the new Clients resource type

getResourceName only resolves friendly names for the Users resource type. For permissions with resourceType "Clients" it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is not set for resources created by getOrCreateResource (only name == client internal id is stored). As a result the admin API/UI will show null (or no name) for client-scoped permissions, instead of the clientId or "All clients". Add a Clients branch resolving the client by id, mirroring the Users handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 (breaking scripted contract)

The exit code signalling "recreate upgrade required" was changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means "feature disabled". Since the documented purpose of this command is to be consumed by scripts/CI pipelines via the exit code, any existing automation keyed on exit code 4 will now interpret a disabled-feature error as "recreate needed" (or miss recreate signals entirely). This should at least be called out in release/upgrade notes, and any other consumers of the constant (e.g. the operator's update logic) verified.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:

false_positives.candidate:
No assertion on the new FEATURE_DISABLED exit code

testFeatureNotEnabled only checks the stderr text and does not assert the process exit code is 4 (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED). Since the exit-code contract is the documented machine-readable interface (and codes were just renumbered), a regression in the exit code would go undetected. Also no test covers the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
canManage() grants manage on groups to admins holding only the view scope

`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the caller only has the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type. `canManage()` backs `requireManage()` used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, so an admin granted only all-groups `view` can create top-level groups. The scope list should contain only `MANAGE` (compare `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79, which correctly uses only `MANAGE`).

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs

In V2, the authz resource created for a group is named with the group id (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, which returns `group.getId()` as the resource name), while `resource.getId()` is an unrelated resource UUID. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and that set is stored as the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. With wrong ids, the store-level filtering/count matches no groups, so user counts are reported as 0 and group-scoped user queries return nothing. Use `groupResource.getName()`.

false_positives.candidate:
Javadoc on requireManageMembers refers to the wrong method

The javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false; the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Also `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` is documented as returning a "Stream of IDs" while its return type is `Set<String>`.

Possible NPE when the Groups resource-type resource cannot be resolved

If `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null (it returns null when the authorization schema is not supported for the resource server, or when the resource type resource is missing), `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` is called with a null resource and `resource.getScopes()` is dereferenced at line 152, causing a NullPointerException instead of a clean deny. Add a null check and return false.

Removal of public ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes breaks extensions

`searchGroupModelsByAttributes` was a public static method on `ModelToRepresentation` in server-spi-private; deleting it is a source/binary incompatible change for any provider or downstream code calling it. Consider deprecating and delegating instead of removing outright, or note the removal in upgrade docs.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes a resource id into hasPermission(groupId, ...)

`hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, but here it is called with `groupResource.getId()` (a resource UUID), not the resource name/group id. The lookup therefore always returns null and the code falls back to the `Groups` resource-type ("all groups") resource, so per-group view-members permissions are never detected and the method returns an empty or incorrect set. Pass `groupResource.getName()` (or refactor to evaluate the already-loaded resource).

getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type

`getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. Group permissions store the group id as the resource name, so for `Groups` permissions this now falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is not set for these resources and will typically be null — the admin console will show no/blank resource name for group permissions. Add a `Groups` branch resolving the group path/name (and "All groups" for the type resource).

true_positives.golden_comment: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Lithuanian translations replaced with Italian text

`loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian) in the Lithuanian bundle; the same wrong-language string was inserted in themes/.../account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101. Lithuanian users will see Italian text. Use a Lithuanian wording (or leave the key out so the English fallback applies).

true_positives.golden_comment: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Simplified Chinese bundle given Traditional Chinese text

`loginTotpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式) in the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle, which is inconsistent with the rest of the file. Should be e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

false_positives.candidate:
Diff reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException

The prefix/suffix trimming computes `start` and `end` independently, so for overlapping cases the subsequent substring calls are invalid. Example: value="aa", sanitized="a" gives start=1 and end=1, then `sanitized.substring(1, 1-1=0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the offending message, the Maven plugin crashes with an unrelated exception. Clamp `end` to `Math.min(end, len-start)` for each string before substring.

Java MessageFormat choice syntax introduced into i18next-based JS message bundles

The admin-ui (and account-ui, line 188 of js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties) bundles are consumed by the React apps through i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders, not Java MessageFormat `{0}`/`{0,choice,...}`. Replacing `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` with `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` means the placeholders are no longer substituted and the raw choice expression is rendered to end users. The sanitizer requirement (avoiding a bare `<`) should be solved differently for the JS bundles, e.g. by keeping `{{n}}` placeholders and avoiding the choice construct.

Missing English counterpart aborts verification with RuntimeException

The English baseline path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, locale suffix -> `_en`). If that file does not exist (community-only themes/locales, or any bundle whose English base lives elsewhere), a RuntimeException is thrown and the whole build fails with "unable to read file ..." rather than the verifier reporting a usable message or skipping the HTML check. Handle FileNotFoundException explicitly (skip or add a descriptive message).

santizeAnchors removes the wrong anchor occurrence / uses stale matcher `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` always strips the *first* textual occurrence of the tag in the (already modified) value, not the occurrence the matcher is currently positioned at, while `matcher` still iterates the original string. For messages with several identical anchor tags (e.g. two ``), tags are removed out of order and positions no longer line up, so legitimate strings can be flagged or malicious extra anchors can slip through unnoticed. Use the matcher's start/end offsets (or build the result with Matcher.appendReplacement) instead of replaceFirst.

true_positives.golden_comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Null check for rawTokenId checks grantType instead

The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it validates `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` passes validation and later produces a token id ending in "null" or an NPE far from the source.

true_positives.golden_comment: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets

In `isAccessTokenId`, the grant shortcut is extracted with `items[0].substring(3, 5)` but the encoded prefix is `<2 chars sessionType><2 chars tokenType><2 chars grantType>`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6. Additionally the check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches. Combined, the matcher accepts tokens with the wrong grant and can reject correct ones, so all event assertions using it (code-to-token, refresh, device, CIBA) do not actually verify the encoded grant type — the new feature is effectively untested.
